label: rare copy-phase feature on late copy steps feeding back y/g/n/w (too sparse)
explanation: Active on only 35 of 1M sequences (21 on dev), with weak magnitudes (max 0.134). Every activation is in the copy phase, on a fed-back token that already appeared in the sequence (in_first = 0). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase. Input tokens are concentrated on y, g, n, w (plus one t), usually at the last or second-to-last copy step. About half the mass is the L=3 case where y is fed back at recall_idx 2 (the final step); the others include w at recall_idx 1 when first_tok = w, and g at recall_idx 4. The partial predicate shown (L=3, y input at recall_idx 2) has about 2% precision. There are too few examples to fit a reliable description.
